# uTLS maintenance

Baseline: official [refraction-networking/utls](https://github.com/refraction-networking/utls/tree/a13c59ffe98bb01b2ca14143eb2e887664b1f138),
commit `a13c59ffe98bb01b2ca14143eb2e887664b1f138`
(`v1.8.3-0.20261108164504-a13c59ffe98b`). Go 1.27+.

The fork supplies generic TLS mechanisms. Browser values and ECH policies live
in Surf. A nil `Config.ECHClientHelloInner` preserves upstream inner construction.
Servers retain upstream behavior.

## Required maintenance policy

Ease of future upstream updates is a design requirement. Preserve upstream
package/file responsibilities, accept compatible structural refactors and keep
fork mechanisms in small owned files with minimal hooks in upstream sources.
Do not maintain obsolete parallel upstream implementations where a small adapter
preserves the required behavior. Keep an explicit inventory of each local
mechanism, hook and reason. Remove superseded adapters only after protocol,
concurrency, public-API and Surf fingerprint/header-order regressions pass.
Browser values and policies belong in Surf; native engine defaults stay intact.

## Required coverage of fork changes

All code changes owned by this fork must have **100% test coverage**, including
existing extensions, new files and changed hooks in upstream sources. Measure
executable additions/modifications against the exact pinned upstream revision;
an overall upstream percentage is not an acceptance criterion. Cover changed
statements and each reachable branch, error, boundary, reset/reuse and
cancellation outcome with meaningful assertions. Go statement coverage alone
must not be presented as proof of branch or protocol-state coverage.

Execute platform-specific behavior on the appropriate OS and combine coverage;
cross-compilation alone is not execution. Types/constants and public API changes
without instrumented statements still need appropriate API/compile/wire checks.
Retain independent browser-source and wire evidence, with actual histories and
normalization limits recorded. Do not exclude owned code, weaken assertions or
change goldens without evidence to obtain the number. Remove obsolete code only
after proving required behavior is preserved. Complete missing coverage before
publishing a new code release; report unmet targets and measurement limits
explicitly rather than claiming 100% prematurely.

Legacy ticket metadata uses a versioned `enetx/tls12-ticket` Extra record and a
read-only `ClientSessionState.TLS12TicketMetadata` accessor. It records original
ServerHello/completion times, the current and known predecessor receipt times,
the unmodified hint and actual resumption/provenance flags. Imported legacy
sessions retain unknown original age. Malformed, duplicate or unknown-version
records are unavailable; unrelated Extra remains opaque. Renewal carries owned
lineage into the fresh session without inheriting stale application Extra.
Public serialization/compression of the same session preserves all Extra.
Clock rollback is a fact, not a codec error. No browser timeout, hint rule or
ticket-renewal policy is embedded in this engine. TLS 1.3 UseBy is unchanged.

Test-only formatting: the certificate generator applies `go/format` before
writing or comparing its fixture, so generated files satisfy the CI format check.

TLS 1.3 certificate authentication hashes the received handshake bytes before
using a decompressed/parsed certificate. Re-marshalling a Certificate can change
its extension order or drop ignored extensions and reject a valid server
signature. Keep the standard Go read/transcript boundary when updating; the
compression helper must not hash the message a second time. Regressions cover
OCSP/SCT order, ignored extensions, CertificateRequest, compression, ordinary
Conn and rejection of altered signatures. References: [Go 1.27.4](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.4/src/crypto/tls/handshake_client_tls13.go),
[Chromium 158's pinned BoringSSL](https://github.com/google/boringssl/blob/ea9f3a34c3977144c45d272be81842fd891a0bdb/ssl/handshake.cc#L166),
[Firefox 160 NSS](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/FIREFOX_160_0_RELEASE/security/nss/lib/ssl/tls13con.c#L4371)
and [RFC 8879](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8879#section-4).

The raw encoder follows RFC 9849 section 6.1 and the upstream discussion in
[uTLS PR #432](https://github.com/refraction-networking/utls/pull/432).
The callback cannot replace key-share cryptography. Outer references must retain
outer order and form one contiguous run; ECH itself cannot be compressed.
The fork validates the private SNI, inner marker and TLS 1.3-only versions with at least one usable TLS 1.3 cipher.
Legacy cipher identifiers may remain advertised, as in NSS; they cannot enable
TLS 1.2 negotiation.

Custom ECH resumption appends an engine-owned PSK last in the inner, binds the
exact expanded transcript (including opaque extensions), and preserves HRR ticket
age/hash decisions. The caller chooses omission or randomized public PSK framing;
real ticket identities and binders never appear in the outer. Outer PSK selection
is rejected after ECH rejection. A nil inner policy retains the upstream custom
ECH/PSK rejection. GREASE-only PSK remains on the original path.

`u_ech_psk.go` owns that mechanism; the session controller retains private session
state without overwriting the outer wire model. `u_early_data.go` emits an optional
QUIC early-data extension only after upstream cipher, ALPN and session-event
checks. HRR removes it before CH2. The early traffic transcript uses the inner
when ECH is offered. Browser extension placement and replay policy live in Surf.

For QUIC, the callback may supply a restricted public transport-parameter offer.
The engine retains its complete parameters in the literal inner extension and
rejects compressed references or changes to its real offer. This does not change
QUIC transport semantics. Surf supplies all filtering rules.

ECH rejection verifies the public outer name (RFC 9849 section 6.1.7). Surf owns
authenticated retry policy; the TLS fork only returns the typed rejection error.

For a caller-supplied ECH inner policy, an explicit `Config.KeyLogWriter` also receives the diagnostic label
`UTLS_ECH_INNER_CLIENT_HELLO <outer-random-hex> <expanded-inner-handshake-hex>`.
This is a nonstandard analysis record containing private SNI, PSK identities and
binders, alongside the traffic secrets already exposed by that writer. Keep the
log private. It observes the already-bound transcript immediately before a send
attempt, including HRR CH2, and never marshals or changes handshake state.
Speculative builds emit no record; writer errors stop the send, like ordinary
key-log errors. No diagnostic inner record is emitted without an explicit writer,
without ECH, or for upstream inner construction (which does not expose a bound
raw transcript at this hook). Standard key-log records retain their behavior.
The same writer receives the standard `CLIENT_EARLY_TRAFFIC_SECRET` record
when QUIC enables early writes. It uses the outer wire random, observes the
existing secret, and propagates writer errors before activating that key.

## Updating

Keep the official Git history and the `upstream` remote. Start from a clean
checkout, fetch the desired official revision, and merge it in a separate
worktree. Resolve the hooks in the table above. Normalize only Go module/import
paths to `github.com/enetx/utls`; preserve upstream source links and licenses.
Update `upstream.json` after reviewing and testing the candidate.

```sh
GOWORK=off go mod tidy
GOWORK=off go test -race -count=1 ./...
GOWORK=off go vet ./...
GOWORK=off go test . -run '^$' -fuzz=FuzzCustomECHInnerRaw -fuzztime=10s
```

Also run Surf's full race/coverage suite against the candidate. Its ECH tests
exercise Chrome and Firefox over TCP and QUIC, native Chrome and Firefox TCP/QUIC inner fixtures,
all initially offered key groups, HRR, verified certificates, policy errors and
application bodies. The fixture report distinguishes native decrypted/callback references from
source-derived assertions. Resumption and early-data tests compare verified
client/server states and early traffic secrets, including HRR and ALPN changes.
